notes.detailedSummary: Reconstructs four separately converging weighted integrals on independent product nets, C_f=2||f||(A.L^(n-1)), the signed raw recursion, exact beta and tent coefficients with minimum c_n for every n, zero-defect measure equivalences, fibre convexity and poles-safe subset polarization. Dual error bounds are conditional on an already known solution.
notes.text:
Lemma1, Theorem2 and Corollary3 receive mathematical PASS relative to n1's exact premises, without modifying the paper.

For actual u,v in E1 put rho_j=MA(u^[n-j],v^[j]), d=v-u on common finite-value representatives, D_j=int d(rho_j-rho_{j+1}), and I=sum D_j=int d(MA(u)-MA(v)). Every integral is finite by O. This is signed raw recursion, with mass V retained.

For continuous endpoints Q_j=theta_u^(n-1-j)theta_v^j and rho_j-rho_{j+1}=-dd^c d Q_j. Therefore D_j=D_Qj(d,d)>=0. Smooth Stokes gives D_Q(a,a)=int da wedge d^c a Q>=0. Symmetry and positivity of D_Q(a+tb,a+tb) give Cauchy-Schwarz. Uniform semipositive regularization passes these statements to continuous differences: signed products expand into finitely many positive products of fixed intersection masses and have uniformly bounded total variation. A uniformly converging multiplying function passes its integral against weakly converging signed products by separating the supnorm-times-TV error from the fixed continuous-test limit.

Write a real PL scalar f=h-k with both FS metrics on the same ample rational A. The positive measures dd^c h Q_j and dd^c k Q_j each have mass (A.L^(n-1)). Consequently 0<=D_Qj(f,f)<=||f||_infinity ||dd^c f Q_j||_TV<=2||f||_infinity(A.L^(n-1))=:C_f. Cauchy-Schwarz proves |int f(rho_j-rho_{j+1})|^2<=C_f D_j, with no ordering assumption on u,v.

For singular endpoints choose independent continuous nets u_a downarrow u and v_b downarrow v on their product directed set. Expand each coefficient into FOUR weighted integrals: int v_b rho_j - int u_a rho_j - int v_b rho_{j+1} + int u_a rho_{j+1}. Every weight and curvature slot decreases on that product. O passes each weighted integral separately to its finite limit. Their signed sum therefore has the claimed nonnegative limit. Weak convergence passes the fixed continuous PL tests, and the uniform C_f estimate survives. No convergence theorem is applied to the nonmonotone difference v_b-u_a, and no singular test curvature on A is defined. Telescoping and finite Cauchy-Schwarz yield |int f(MA(u)-MA(v))|^2<=n C_f I.

Let g(t)=E((1-t)u+tv). The actual finite segment polynomial and derivative give -g''(t)=n sum_{j=0}^{n-1} binom(n-1,j)t^j(1-t)^(n-1-j)D_j. The same four-integral passage also justifies its coefficients. For B_u(v)=E(u)-E(v)+int(v-u)MA(u), two integrations give B_u(v)=int_0^1(1-t)(-g'')dt and B_v(u)=int_0^1 t(-g'')dt. Repeated integration by parts gives the integer beta integral a!b!/(a+b+1)!. Hence B_u(v)=sum (n-j)D_j/(n+1), B_v(u)=sum (j+1)D_j/(n+1), I/(n+1)<=B_u(v)<=nI/(n+1), and B_u(v)+B_v(u)=I. There is no extra mass or factorial normalization.

For Delta=g(1/2)-(g(0)+g(1))/2, G(t)=min(t,1-t)/2 vanishes at the endpoints and has derivative jump -1. Piecewise integration by parts gives Delta=sum alpha_{n,j}D_j, with alpha_{n,j}=n binom(n-1,j)int G(t)t^j(1-t)^(n-1-j)dt.

The exact minimum is proved for every n, independently of finite checks. Put b_{m,j}=binom(m,j)t^j(1-t)^(m-j). Symmetry gives alpha_j=alpha_{n-1-j}. The identity b'_{n,j+1}=n(b_{n-1,j}-b_{n-1,j+1}) implies alpha_{j+1}-alpha_j=(int_0^(1/2)b_{n,j+1}-int_(1/2)^1 b_{n,j+1})/2. When j+1<=n/2, the ratio b(t)/b(1-t)=(t/(1-t))^(2(j+1)-n)>=1 for 0<t<=1/2. Thus the coefficients increase toward the middle and decrease by symmetry; their minimum is an endpoint. Evaluate that endpoint with the formal polynomial g=-(1-t)^(n+1)/(n+1): its midpoint deficit is (1/2-2^(-(n+1)))/(n+1)=(1-2^(-n))/(2(n+1))=:c_n. This proves the minimum for every integer n>=1, in particular every retained n>=2. It is a coefficient calculation, not an actual metric example. Therefore Delta>=c_n I and |int f(MA(u)-MA(v))|^2<=n C_f Delta/c_n.

If I=0, every nonnegative D_j vanishes. The individual PL bound makes each rho_j-rho_{j+1} annihilate all PL tests. Uniform density and TV<=2V extend this to all continuous tests and identify the signed Radon measures as zero. Conversely equal pure measures make the defining finite integral I zero. Positive alpha also give Delta=0 iff I=0. Zero I, zero Delta, equality of pure measures and equality of all successive mixed measures are therefore equivalent MEASURE statements. They do not determine all-point potential values, including common poles.

For a common pure-measure fibre, the binomial curvature formula and successive mixed-measure equality show every segment stays in the fibre; induction gives finite convex combinations. For w1,...,wn in that fibre, every nonempty subset average w_S is actual E1 and has the same pure measure. O's polarization is MA(w1,...,wn)=1/n! sum_{S nonempty}(-1)^(n-|S|)|S|^n MA(w_S). Inclusion-exclusion counts onto maps on n labels and gives coefficient sum one. The mixed measure is consequently the same pure measure. Repeated slots are allowed; zero coefficients are omitted at poles; no empty-subset potential or zero-times-infinity is evaluated.

Corollary3 first assumes a genuine solution MA(u)=mu. O then supplies its intrinsic integrability, and M supplies finite dual and attainment F_mu(u)=J. Only after this antecedent does epsilon_mu(v)=J-F_mu(v)=B_u(v). Thus I/(n+1)<=epsilon_mu(v)<=nI/(n+1), and |int f(MA(v)-mu)|^2<=n(n+1)C_f epsilon_mu(v). Mixed outputs of actual solutions equal mu by the fibre argument. This proves stability at an existing solution and does not construct the initial solution.

notes.text:
Theorem4, Proposition5, reference covariance and retained scope receive mathematical PASS relative to n1 and n2.

For an intrinsic positive Radon target mu of raw mass V, every actual E1 scalar is absolutely mu-integrable and J is finite. Constants cancel in F_mu=E-int u mu, since E(u+c)=E(u)+cV. M identifies continuous and all-E1 suprema, so epsilon_mu(u)=J-F_mu(u)>=0 is finite. F_mu(0)=0 gives J>=0.

The integral term is affine on actual segments. Hence Delta(u,v)=F_mu((u+v)/2)-(F_mu(u)+F_mu(v))/2<=(epsilon(u)+epsilon(v))/2. Applying n2 gives equation (14): |int f(MA(u)-MA(v))|^2<=[nC_f/(2c_n)](epsilon(u)+epsilon(v)).

Choose continuous u_k with epsilon(u_k)<=1/k from the finite real supremum. This is ordinary maximizing-sequence selection, not a cofinal sequence for FS approximation nets or the analytic carrier. Their output integrals are Cauchy on each PL test. For f in C(T), choose PL p uniformly close; the error against two positive mass-V outputs is at most 2V||f-p||. Thus their f-integrals are Cauchy. The limits form a positive linear functional L on C(T), with |L(f)|<=V||f|| and L(1)=V. Compact Hausdorff positive-functional Riesz representation gives a unique positive regular Radon lambda of mass V. No metrizability, separability, first countability or countable cofinality is assumed.

For another maximizing net, compare it with the fixed sequence using (14). For a fixed PL test, first choose a sequence term with small error and small scalar-limit error, then choose a net tail with small error. This gives the same PL limits; uniform density and mass give weak convergence on every continuous test. Comparing one fixed u against the sequence gives equation (12): |int f(MA(u)-lambda)|^2<=[nC_f/(2c_n)]epsilon(u). No potential limit has been constructed.

For intrinsic energy of lambda, work solely in M's selected original reference. Sup-normalize one maximizing sequence by finite constants, preserving F and epsilon. Its actual endpoints have finite suprema. A tail has F>=-1. With finite U=U_mu, d_n=n(n+1)/2, C=U(1+2M0), a=U sqrt(2d_n), M gives -1<=-B+C+a sqrt(B). Setting s=sqrt(B)>=0 gives s^2-a s-(C+1)<=0, hence B<=R=[(a+sqrt(a^2+4(C+1)))/2]^2. This is the exact quadratic root, including U=0. Reference moment alone does not provide this target coercivity.

For every normalized actual w in E1, O with all n slots equal to u_k gives int(-w)MA(u_k)<=H_n[B(w)+nB(u_k)]<=H_n[B(w)+nR], H_n=(n+1)^(n+1)/n!. The function -w is nonnegative lower semicontinuous and may be infinite at poles.

The integral passage is valid for arbitrary compact Hausdorff Radon measures. For g>=0 lower semicontinuous and finite positive Radon nu, int g dnu is the supremum of int h dnu over continuous 0<=h<=g. To see this, approximate min(g,N) from below by finitely many strict open superlevels, choose inner compact subsets of those levels, and use normality to construct continuous cutoffs equal to one on the compact subsets and supported in the superlevels. Their weighted sum is a continuous minorant; inner regularity makes its integral close to the step integral. Refine levels and let N increase. Each fixed continuous minorant passes through weak convergence, yielding int g dnu<=liminf_i int g dnu_i. This argument works for nets and does not require a metric topology. Applied to -w it proves equation (13): int(-w)lambda<=H_n[B(w)+nR].

Finite constant shifts now give absolute integrability of every unnormalized actual E1 scalar against lambda. Positivity, Radon regularity and mass V were already proved. ONLY NOW does M apply to lambda, giving its intrinsic condition and finite J. Equation (13) directly gives U_lambda<=H_n(1+nR), and M gives J(lambda)<=U_lambda(1+2M0)+(d_n/2)U_lambda^2. These statements do not assume lambda is an actual output.

For mixed convergence, choose n slots from finitely many maximizing nets on their product directed set. Every nonempty subset average is actual E1 and, by concavity, has error at most the average of its slots' errors, tending to zero. Its pure output converges to lambda. Finite polarization and the coefficient sum one from n2 give convergence of the genuine mixed output to lambda. Constant maximizing nets identify the pure outputs of actual maximizers with lambda; their mixed outputs agree by fibre rigidity. An already known genuine solution is a maximizer by M, so its constant output gives lambda=mu only in that conditional case.

For psi'=psi+b, b is bounded continuous. Absolute potentials correspond as u'=u-b. O gives E_psi'(u')=E_psi(u)-E_psi(b), and therefore F_psi',mu(u')=F_psi,mu(u)-E_psi(b)+int b dmu. The same finite correction changes J, preserving epsilon. Absolute genuine outputs are unchanged, so corresponding maximizing nets have the same lambda. No moment atoms are moved or asserted at the new reference. Equation (13) remains selected-reference only.

For Proposition5, all actual-competitor integrals int(v-u)[MA(u)-mu] are finite on common finite-value sets. The actual segment derivative of F at zero is this integral. A maximum makes every such one-sided derivative nonpositive. Conversely concavity gives F(v)-F(u)<=that derivative; the inequalities imply the all-E1 supremum, which M identifies with J. This proves equation (15). The directions are toward psh competitors. Both signs of an arbitrary continuous test need not be admissible, so PL density cannot turn these inequalities into equality of measures.

All three original gaps remain OPEN: actual E1 maximizing-potential attainment for every intrinsic target; lambda_mu=mu for every target or complete actual envelope/orthogonality/both-sign differentiation replacements; and I(u,v)=0 implying u=v+c at EVERY analytic point for one finite constant, including common poles, hence EVERY-solution EVERY-point uniqueness. If the first two were proved, a constant maximizing net would give the equation; the third would give the required uniqueness. None is established here. Finite-U coercivity does not prove actual psh closure or potential compactness. Weak measure limits do not supply potentials. C comparison and D descent do not fill these gaps. T and S remain their already granted trivial-field and curve sectors; no n>=2 curve extrapolation, abstract closure or inverse-defined operator is imported.
